question.problem:
Let $X=[{X}_{1},{X}_{2},{X}_{3}]^{T}$ be a multivariate normal random vector with mean vector $\mu $ and covariance matrix $Σ$ given by

$$
\begin{aligned}\mu =[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 3 \\ 2\end{aligned}],\,Σ=[\begin{aligned}3 & 2 & 1 \\ 2 & 4 & 2 \\ 1 & 2 & 5\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Find the distribution of $Y=-{X}_{1}+3{X}_{2}+2{X}_{3}.$
question.worked_solution:
Recall that if $X=[{X}_{1},{X}_{2},…,{X}_{k}]^{T}$ is a multivariate normal random vector with mean vector $\mu $ and covariance matrix $Σ,$ then the random variable $Y,$ defined as

$$
Y={c}^{T}X={\sum }_{i=1}^{k}{c}_{i}{X}_{i}
$$

is a normally distributed random variable, where $c$ is any $k\times 1$ column vector, and  

$$
\begin{aligned}E[Y] & ={c}^{T}\mu , \\ Var[Y] & ={c}^{T}Σc.\end{aligned}
$$

In our case, since we wish to know the distribution of $Y=-{X}_{1}+3{X}_{2}+2{X}_{3},$ we have 

$$
c=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 3 \\ 2\end{aligned}].
$$

Therefore, for the mean of $Y,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[Y] & ={c}^{T}\mu  \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-1 & 3 & 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 \\ 3 \\ 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =0+9+4 \\  & =13,\end{aligned}
$$

and for the variance of $Y,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Var}[Y] & ={c}^{T}Σc \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-1 & 3 & 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}3 & 2 & 1 \\ 2 & 4 & 2 \\ 1 & 2 & 5\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 3 \\ 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-1 & 3 & 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}5 \\ 14 \\ 15\end{aligned}] \\  & =-5+42+30 \\  & =67.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we conclude that

$$
Y∼N(13,67).
$$
